Location: Figure 1, arrow 1; Section 4.1, Phase I item 1
Verbatim: Attacker’s client queries the victim resolver about xyz.referral.com
Normalized: Attacker Client -> Recursive Resolver: 'A' query xyz.referral.com [DNS; qtype=A, qname=xyz.referral.com]

Location: Figure 1, arrow 2; Section 4.1, Phase I item 2
Normalized: Recursive Resolver -> .referral.com name servers: 'A' query xyz.referral.com [DNS; qtype=A]

Location: Figure 1, arrow 3; Section 4.1, Phase I item 3
Verbatim: Authoritative referral.com responds with a large referral response (LRR)
Normalized: .referral.com name servers -> Recursive Resolver: Referral Response carrying n NS records and no glue [DNS; authority=n NS, additional=0]

Location: Figure 1, box 4; Section 4.1, Phase II item 1
Verbatim: The resolver looks up each of the n names to see if any one of them already has a resolution it can use. This is a total of 2n lookups. This step is the core source of the high complexity, especially since it will be repeated many times, as explained in the next phase
Normalized: Recursive Resolver -> Recursive Resolver: process the referral response and look up each of the n NS names in cache and ADB, 2n lookups [none; internal]

Location: Figure 1, box 5; Section 4.1, Phase II items 2 and 3
Verbatim: n > referral-limit, start only referral-limit* new resolution processes and Turn on “No_Fetch” flag
Normalized: Recursive Resolver -> Recursive Resolver: start referral-limit new resolution processes and set the No_Fetch flag [none; internal, referral-limit=5 in BIND9]

Location: Figure 1, arrow 6; Section 4.1, Phase II item 4
Verbatim: The resolver issues the query for these referral-limit NS names
Normalized: Recursive Resolver -> .delegation.com name servers: 'A' query for the referral-limit NS names [DNS; qtype=A, 5 in parallel]

Location: Figure 1, arrow 7; Section 4.1, Phase III item 1
Verbatim: Each such name leads the resolver to an authoritative, which responds with a server IP address that is non-responsive to DNS queries and issues the delegation response
Normalized: .delegation.com name servers -> Recursive Resolver: 'A' response delegating to the address of a server that does not answer DNS [DNS; answer A = non-responsive host]

Location: Figure 1, box 8; Section 4.1, Phase III item 2
Verbatim: Upon receiving a delegation response, the resolver triggers a restart event and restarts the resolution for the LRR
Normalized: Recursive Resolver -> Recursive Resolver: trigger a restart event and restart the LRR resolution [none; internal]

Location: Figure 1, box 9; Section 4.1, Phase III item 3
Verbatim: The victim resolver clears the “No_Fetch” flag
Normalized: Recursive Resolver -> Recursive Resolver: clear the No_Fetch flag [none; internal]

Location: Figure 1, arrow 10; Section 4.1, Phase III item 4(a)
Normalized: Recursive Resolver -> Recursive Resolver: restart processing of the referral record list [none; internal]

Location: Figure 1, arrow 11; Section 4.1, Phase III item 4(b)
Normalized: Recursive Resolver -> Non-Responsive to DNS queries: 'A' query xyz.referral.com [DNS; qtype=A, 5 in parallel]

Location: Figure 1, arrow 12; Section 4.1, Phase III item 4(b)
Normalized: Non-Responsive to DNS queries -> Recursive Resolver: nothing is returned [none; absence of a reply]

Location: Figure 1, arrow 13; Section 4.1, Phase III item 6
Verbatim: The victim loops through Phases II and III until a timeout or restart limit is reached and a ’FAIL’ response is returned to the client
Normalized: Recursive Resolver -> Attacker Client: 'FAIL' response for xyz.referral.com after the restart limit or a timeout [DNS; rcode=SERVFAIL]
